skills.name: Refactoring UI
skills.summary: Make interfaces look consistent and intentional: spacing, color, hierarchy, and reusable visual rules.
skills.use_when: Use when the UI works but looks uneven, cluttered, or “generated.”

skills.name: iOS HIG Design
skills.summary: Design iPhone and iPad interfaces using Apple’s platform conventions for navigation, controls, accessibility, and layout.
skills.use_when: Use when building or reviewing an Apple-platform app.

skills.name: UX Heuristics
skills.summary: Review screens for common usability problems such as unclear labels, weak feedback, or unnecessary memory load.
skills.use_when: Use when people get lost, abandon forms, or need help to complete tasks.

skills.name: Web Typography
skills.summary: Choose readable type, line length, hierarchy, and web font loading approaches.
skills.use_when: Use for content-heavy sites or when text is hard to read.

skills.name: Design of Everyday Things
skills.summary: Make controls understandable through clear affordances, feedback, and sensible mapping.
skills.use_when: Use when users click the wrong thing or don’t know what a control does.

skills.name: Top Design
skills.summary: Push a polished web design toward a distinctive, memorable art direction.
skills.use_when: Use for launch pages or brand moments after clarity and usability are sound.

skills.name: Lean UX
skills.summary: Turn assumptions about a feature into small, testable design experiments.
skills.use_when: Use when the team might be building the wrong experience.

skills.name: Microinteractions
skills.summary: Design feedback for small actions: saving, loading, errors, toggles, and transitions.
skills.use_when: Use when an app feels unresponsive or small actions lack clear feedback.

skills.name: Steve Jobs Design Review
skills.summary: Run a sharp final product/design critique that surfaces weak details and a concrete cut list.
skills.use_when: Use before launch or review when “good enough” needs a clear verdict.

skills.name: StoryBrand Messaging
skills.summary: Explain a product clearly by framing the customer as the main character and the company as a guide.
skills.use_when: Use when the homepage talks about the company but visitors don’t understand the benefit.

skills.name: Made to Stick
skills.summary: Make ideas clearer and easier to remember using concrete, credible examples and stories.
skills.use_when: Use when people hear the pitch but can’t repeat it later.

skills.name: Contagious
skills.summary: Find product or message features that give people a reason to talk about and share them.
skills.use_when: Use when referrals or word of mouth are an important growth channel.

skills.name: 1-Page Marketing Plan
skills.summary: Map marketing from target audience through lead capture, sales, retention, and referrals.
skills.use_when: Use when marketing is a loose set of tactics without a connected plan.

skills.name: Scorecard Marketing
skills.summary: Create a scored assessment or quiz that gives prospects a useful result and helps qualify leads.
skills.use_when: Use when a generic downloadable guide is not attracting useful leads.

skills.name: Obviously Awesome
skills.summary: Clarify category, target customer, alternatives, and differentiated value.
skills.use_when: Use when prospects don’t understand what the product replaces or why it is different.

skills.name: $100M Offers
skills.summary: Improve the package, value, guarantees, and presentation of an offer.
skills.use_when: Use when qualified buyers see the offer as too expensive or incomplete. Validate price first.

skills.name: Negotiation
skills.summary: Prepare for difficult sales or partnership conversations using listening, calibrated questions, and structured offers.
skills.use_when: Use for high-stakes negotiations, not routine messages.

skills.name: Influence Psychology
skills.summary: Understand persuasion principles and apply them ethically to pages, emails, and onboarding.
skills.use_when: Use when people need trust or motivation; avoid fake scarcity or manipulative pressure.

skills.name: Predictable Revenue
skills.summary: Build a repeatable outbound sales pipeline and work backwards from revenue goals.
skills.use_when: Use when sales depend on luck or founder-only networking.

skills.name: CRO Methodology
skills.summary: Diagnose conversion problems and prioritize changes as testable hypotheses.
skills.use_when: Use when traffic is arriving but people fail to take the intended next step.

skills.name: Monetizing Innovation
skills.summary: Research willingness to pay and design product/price choices around customer value.
skills.use_when: Use before or during product development, before settling on a price.

skills.name: Jobs to Be Done
skills.summary: Understand what progress customers are trying to make and what they use instead.
skills.use_when: Use when deciding what problem a product or feature should solve.

skills.name: Hooked UX
skills.summary: Analyze a product’s cue, action, reward, and investment loop.
skills.use_when: Use when repeat use is part of genuine user value; don’t manufacture compulsive use.

skills.name: Improve Retention
skills.summary: Apply behavior design to help users repeat a beneficial action with manageable prompts and ability.
skills.use_when: Use when users try the product but do not return or complete the core habit.

skills.name: Lean Startup
skills.summary: Test risky business assumptions through short build-measure-learn experiments.
skills.use_when: Use when an idea is uncertain and a full build would be costly.

skills.name: Design Sprint
skills.summary: Run a time-boxed process to map a problem, sketch, choose, prototype, and test with users.
skills.use_when: Use when a team needs evidence on one focused product question quickly.

skills.name: Continuous Discovery
skills.summary: Make customer interviews and opportunity testing a regular product practice.
skills.use_when: Use when research happens only in occasional projects or roadmaps lack evidence.

skills.name: Inspired
skills.summary: Organize product work around customer problems and discovery before delivery commitments.
skills.use_when: Use when teams are given feature lists without a clear outcome or product strategy.

skills.name: The Mom Test
skills.summary: Ask customer interview questions that reveal real past behavior instead of polite opinions.
skills.use_when: Use before building or when validating demand.

skills.name: The 37signals Way
skills.summary: Keep product scope small, work in appetite-bounded chunks, and avoid unnecessary process.
skills.use_when: Use when plans keep expanding or projects have no clear finish line.

skills.name: Lean Analytics
skills.summary: Choose a meaningful metric and a threshold that should change a decision.
skills.use_when: Use when dashboards are full but nobody knows whether progress is real.

skills.name: Crossing the Chasm
skills.summary: Choose a focused customer segment to move from early adopters toward mainstream adoption.
skills.use_when: Use when early enthusiasts buy but the next market segment does not.

skills.name: Blue Ocean Strategy
skills.summary: Find value customers want that avoids competing only on the same factors as rivals.
skills.use_when: Use in crowded markets where competition mostly drives price down.

skills.name: Cold Start Problem
skills.summary: Plan how a network product gets its first useful users on each side and reaches critical mass.
skills.use_when: Use for marketplaces, social products, or other products that need participants to be valuable.

skills.name: Good Strategy Bad Strategy
skills.summary: Turn a vague ambition into a diagnosis, guiding policy, and coordinated actions.
skills.use_when: Use when priorities are numerous but the actual constraint is unclear.

skills.name: Traction EOS
skills.summary: Set company priorities, owners, scorecards, and a regular operating meeting rhythm.
skills.use_when: Use when a sufficiently sized business needs consistent execution and accountability.

skills.name: Drive Motivation
skills.summary: Review whether work supports autonomy, mastery, and purpose rather than relying only on rewards.
skills.use_when: Use when motivation or initiative is slipping; pair with real conversations.

skills.name: High Output Management
skills.summary: Improve manager leverage, delegation, one-to-ones, and team operating practices.
skills.use_when: Use when a manager is a bottleneck or the team’s time is not producing enough output.

skills.name: Team Topologies
skills.summary: Shape team boundaries and interaction patterns to reduce handoffs and cognitive overload.
skills.use_when: Use when work gets stuck across several engineering teams.

skills.name: Clean Code
skills.summary: Improve names, functions, errors, and readability so code is easier to understand.
skills.use_when: Use when code works but is confusing or costly to review.

skills.name: Pragmatic Programmer
skills.summary: Apply practical engineering habits such as reducing duplicated knowledge and proving paths end to end.
skills.use_when: Use as broad guidance for building and maintaining software.

skills.name: Refactoring
skills.summary: Restructure code in small behavior-preserving steps.
skills.use_when: Use when tests exist and the code’s structure needs to improve.

skills.name: Software Design
skills.summary: Reduce complexity by designing modules that hide difficult details behind useful interfaces.
skills.use_when: Use when every change touches too many parts or abstractions make the system harder.

skills.name: Legacy Code
skills.summary: Find safe seams and capture current behavior before changing untested code.
skills.use_when: Use before modifying old code that has little or no test coverage.

skills.name: Clean Architecture
skills.summary: Keep core business rules testable and independent from frameworks and databases.
skills.use_when: Use when the framework must boot just to test a business rule or infrastructure is hard to replace.

skills.name: Domain-Driven Design
skills.summary: Model complicated business rules and define boundaries with a shared vocabulary.
skills.use_when: Use when one model or class is trying to represent different parts of the business.

skills.name: Data-Intensive Apps
skills.summary: Reason about databases, replication, consistency, partitioning, and data pipelines.
skills.use_when: Use when concurrent updates, stale reads, storage choice, or hot partitions matter.

skills.name: System Design
skills.summary: Estimate traffic, storage, and major components before building a system.
skills.use_when: Use when planning capacity or designing a system that may serve significant traffic.

skills.name: Release It!
skills.summary: Protect production services with timeouts, retries, circuit breakers, resource limits, and health checks.
skills.use_when: Use whenever the app depends on networks or external services, especially before launch.

skills.name: High Perf Browser
skills.summary: Improve the time between a browser request and a usable page using networking and resource loading choices.
skills.use_when: Use when the backend is responsive but the browser page still paints slowly.

journeys.name: Create an App
journeys.tagline: Idea → validated app with deliberate architecture
journeys.fits: new app idea to validate and give sound foundations

journeys.name: Improve a Business
journeys.tagline: Diagnose and address a plateaued business

journeys.tagline: Find and fix evidence-backed website problems

journeys.name: Improve an App
journeys.tagline: Improve product fit, usability, copy, and experience
journeys.fits: live app whose product fit, usability or copy is weak

journeys.name: Grow a Business
journeys.tagline: Build a repeatable marketing and sales engine
journeys.fits: business that needs a repeatable marketing and sales engine

journeys.name: Grow a Website
journeys.tagline: Convert more existing traffic and capture leads
journeys.fits: site with traffic that should convert and capture more leads

journeys.name: Grow an App
journeys.tagline: Improve activation, retention, and ongoing product learning
journeys.fits: existing product that users try but don't stick with

journeys.name: Improve Code Quality
journeys.tagline: Harden a prototype into maintainable production code

journeys.name: Remove Technical Debt
journeys.tagline: Make legacy code safer to change while continuing to ship
journeys.fits: legacy code that needs safe incremental cleanup

journeys.name: Design Code Architecture
journeys.tagline: Choose boundaries, data, scale, and resilience for a new system
journeys.fits: new system that needs its boundaries, data and scale chosen

journeys.name: Conversion Optimization
journeys.tagline: Diagnose one leaking conversion flow and test improvements
journeys.fits: one funnel or flow that leaks conversions

journeys.name: Architecture Optimization
journeys.tagline: Improve a slow, tangled codebase with targeted performance and boundaries
journeys.fits: slow, tangled codebase that needs targeted fixes

routes.note: Add iOS HIG only for an iPhone/iPad app.

routes.name: Build a small local service website
routes.note: Avoid loading every architecture skill for a simple brochure site.

routes.name: Improve an online shop with abandoned checkout
routes.note: Use the focused Conversion Optimization journey for one funnel.

routes.name: Stabilize a prototype before launch
steps: add a safety net if untested
routes.note: Give the agent the actual expected traffic; don’t design for imaginary scale.

routes.name: Safely change a mature legacy system
steps: find seams and capture current behavior
routes.note: Keep changes small and review them as you go.

routes.name: Help a B2B product grow beyond early adopters
Improve a mobile app’s retention
routes.note: Optimize for lasting user value, not engagement for its own sake.

routes.name: Organize a growing engineering team
steps: add an operating rhythm if company size fits
routes.note: Use the team-size-appropriate parts; the source cautions that EOS can be too much machinery for a very small team.
